open_points.subject: MCP entrance and request framing
open_points.text: “serve the one MCP entrance” and “its size, counted as the bytes of the request message as received”
open_points.question: Which MCP transport and protocol version does the listener implement, where is the authentication token carried, and exactly which received bytes count toward surface_request_bytes_max?
options: MCP Streamable HTTP with the token in an Authorization header and the encoded message body counted
MCP Streamable HTTP with the token inside each operation payload and the whole payload counted
A non-HTTP JSON-RPC transport defined by the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Use MCP Streamable HTTP behind the reverse proxy, carry the token as an Authorization bearer token, and count the encoded MCP request body.

open_points.subject: Mapped value element references
open_points.text: “A value list is one StoredValue, the JSON array of the elements' values” and “the element's inputs by port as references — StoredValues and SpooledFiles”
open_points.question: When a mapped node consumes one element of a many value stored only as one array StoredValue, what durable reference represents that scalar element in its NodeExecution, approval preview and EffectAttempt inputs, and which named store change creates it?
options: Materialize one StoredValue per mapped element when the list is delivered
Refer to the parent StoredValue together with an array index, requiring that reference form in the models
Keep the element only as derived inline data and use no StoredValue reference
open_points.default_guess: Materialize a StoredValue for each mapped value element, with the mapped input port's element schema and the list's disclosure class, when the list is delivered.

open_points.subject: Effect idempotency key
open_points.text: “The EffectAttempt's idempotency_key is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of those fields' values”
open_points.question: What JSON value is hashed when several idempotency-key fields are declared: an object keyed by field name, an ordered array of values, or another structure?
options: An object mapping every declared field name to its value
An array of values in manifest field order
An array of name-value pairs in manifest field order
open_points.default_guess: Hash a JSON object mapping field names to their values; JCS then fixes key ordering.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision access
open_points.text: “manifest_location, manifest_revision: where the platform manifest is read and the repository revision it is read at”
open_points.question: How must bindings read a service record at manifest_revision without changing the working tree, and what precisely proves that the bytes came from that revision?
options: Read the file directly from a Git object at the named revision
Require manifest_location to be an already checked-out tree and verify its current revision
Use an installation-provided immutable snapshot resolver
open_points.default_guess: Read the service file directly from the Git object named by manifest_revision without checking out or modifying the repository.

open_points.subject: Service base URL
open_points.text: “an absolute http or https URL with a host” and “The URL is the api_base_url without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path”
open_points.question: May api_base_url contain user information, a query, a fragment, or a path prefix, and does removing a trailing slash remove one slash or all trailing slashes?
options: Allow only scheme, authority and an optional path prefix; forbid user information, query and fragment
Allow any absolute URL with a host and apply textual concatenation
Allow only an origin with no path, query, fragment or user information
open_points.default_guess: Allow an optional path prefix, forbid user information, query and fragment, remove all trailing slashes from the prefix, then append the declared path.

open_points.subject: Token-list recovery after an invalid reread
open_points.text: “When any fails, every request is refused ... until a re-read passes” and “re-read when the file's digest changed or it cannot be read”
open_points.question: After a readable changed file fails token-list validation, must current_token_list retry parsing it on every request while no valid list exists, or only after its bytes change again?
options: Retry every request while there is no valid token list
Cache the failed file digest and retry only after its bytes change
Retain a watcher or explicit invalidation signal that triggers the retry
open_points.default_guess: Keep the last valid digest as the comparison baseline and retry every request until a valid token list is obtained.

open_points.subject: Existing store schema at startup
open_points.text: “the database schema ... [is] created inside the data directory when absent”
open_points.question: What does open_store do when the SQLite database exists but has an unknown, older, newer, incomplete or corrupt schema?
options: Refuse startup without modifying it
Run defined in-place migrations
Treat it as internal_error and stop
Replace or recreate it
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup without modifying the database; this kernel defines no migration or destructive recreation operation.

open_points.subject: Service failure detail without a usable response
open_points.text: “One outcome name ... and a bounded failure_detail” and “The body of an answer that is not used is not interpreted; at most failure_detail_bytes_max of it is kept as failure_detail”
open_points.question: What failure_detail is returned for DNS, connection, TLS, timeout, reset, EOF or malformed-response outcomes where no response body is available?
options: No failure_detail
A fixed detail per transport category
A sanitized transport-library message
open_points.default_guess: Return no failure_detail when no response body is available, avoiding unstable or host-revealing transport text.

open_points.subject: Masked failure-detail length
open_points.text: “returned to an agent only as its length and that class”
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length of a classified failure_detail measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
options: UTF-8 bytes
Unicode code points
Characters after truncation as defined by the runtime
open_points.default_guess: Report UTF-8 byte length, matching failure_detail_bytes_max and the truncation rule.
